title: The four winds — the Hebrew says “I have spread you abroad”, the Greek says “I will gather you”

Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Zechariah 9:10: Καὶ ἐξολοθρεύσει ἅρματα ἐξ Ἐφραὶμ, καὶ ἵππον ἐξ Ἱερουσαλὴμ, καὶ ἐξολοθρεύσεται τόξον πολεμικὸν, καὶ πλῆθος καὶ εἰρήνη ἐξ ἐθνῶν, καὶ κατάρξει ὑδάτων ἕως θαλάσσης, καὶ ποταμῶν διεκβολὰς γῆς. [and the multitude and peace from the nations, and he shall rule over waters as far as the sea, and over the outlets of rivers of the land]. Brenton English Zechariah 9:10: “And he shall destroy the chariots out of Ephraim, and the horse out of Jerusalem, and the bow of war shall be utterly destroyed; and there shall be abundance and peace out of the nations; and he shall rule over the waters as far as the sea, and the rivers to the ends of the earth.” Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/ZEC09.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/38/9/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/ZEC09.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/ZEC09.htm.
reasoning: In the Hebrew the king speaks peace to the nations, and his rule runs from sea to sea and from the river to the ends of the earth. In the Greek the phrase is “multitude and peace out of the nations”, which can be read as something taken from the nations or as part of the list of what is cut off, and the rule is described in terms of waters, the sea, rivers and the land. The KJV’s declaration of peace to the nations is not stated in the Greek in the same way.

title: “Prisoners of hope” in the Hebrew — “prisoners of the gathering” in the Greek
summary: The KJV calls the people “prisoners of hope” and tells them to turn to the strong hold. The Hebrew is אֲסִירֵי הַתִּקְוָה. Brenton’s Greek is δέσμιοι τῆς συναγωγῆς, “prisoners of the synagogue (assembly)”, and says they will sit in strongholds.
text: KJV Zechariah 9:12: “Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope: even to day do I declare that I will render double unto thee;” Hebrew (WLC) Zechariah 9:12: וּבוּ לְבִצָּרֹ֔ון אֲסִירֵ֖י הַתִּקְוָ֑ה גַּם־הַיֹּ֕ום מַגִּ֥יד מִשְׁנֶ֖ה אָשִׁ֥יב לָֽךְ׃ [return to a stronghold, prisoners of the hope; even today I declare, I will return double to you]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Zechariah 9:12: Καθήσεσθε ἐν ὀχυρώμασι δέσμιοι τῆς συναγωγῆς, καὶ ἀντὶ μιᾶς ἡμέρας παροικεσίας σου διπλᾶ ἀνταποδώσω σοι, [you will sit in strongholds, prisoners of the assembly, and in return for one day of your sojourn I will render you double]. Brenton English Zechariah 9:12: “Ye shall dwell in strongholds, ye prisoners of the congregation: and for one day of thy captivity I will recompense thee double.” Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/ZEC09.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/38/9/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/ZEC09.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/ZEC09.htm.
reasoning: The Hebrew word תִּקְוָה means hope (or a cord); the Greek συναγωγή means an assembly or gathering. The KJV addresses the prisoners with a command to turn to the stronghold; the Greek has a future statement that they will sit in strongholds. The Greek also adds the reason for the double: in return for one day of their sojourn.
scope: T applies at Zechariah 9:12, Septuagint only. The KJV agrees with the Hebrew and no Hebrew mistranslation is claimed. The record states the two expressions and does not say which is original or what the assembly is. The Greek “in return for one day of your sojourn” stands where the Hebrew has “even today”; the record notes this and draws no conclusion from it.
